explanation: Secondary prevention is all about catching things early! Think of screenings and prompt treatments that stop a small infection from turning into a major emergency. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T79#GNS214_U1_T79_h7)

question: What is a main goal of counseling a patient *before* they take an STI test?

options.A: Administering therapeutic antibiotics before laboratory confirmation returns
options.B: Explaining test procedures and infection window periods to the client
options.C: Providing the client with their final laboratory test results immediately
options.D: Forcing the client to disclose the names of all past sexual partners

explanation: Pre-test counseling helps prep the patient so they know what to expect and understand why timing (the window period) is everything. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T3#GNS216_U5_T3_h5)

question: What is the best way to tell if a food safety training program actually worked?

options.A: Watching to see if workers practice safe habits on the kitchen floor
options.B: Making sure everyone memorized the manual word-for-word
options.C: Calculating how much money was spent on the workshop
options.D: Checking that everyone sat through every minute of the lecture

explanation: Real learning shows in daily habits! True success is when staff actually use what they learned while cooking and cleaning. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h8)

question: What is the main goal of injection safety protocols in nursing?

options.A: To prevent harm to patients and protect healthcare workers
options.B: To ensure medications are absorbed faster by the body
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing new syringes
options.D: To speed up medication administration during busy shifts

explanation: Injection safety is all about keeping both sides safe—protecting the patient receiving the injection and keeping you, the nurse, safe from injuries and infections! [learn more](GNS122_U4_T4#GNS122_U4_T4_h1)

question: What do hospital executives usually care about most when reviewing data?

options.A: Cost efficiency and regulatory compliance
options.B: Detailed patient bedside vital sign charts
options.C: Brand names of intravenous catheters used
options.D: Personal shift schedules for junior staff

explanation: Well done! Hospital leaders look at the big picture—budgets, laws, and keeping the hospital safe and running smoothly. [learn more](GST319_U1_T2#GST319_U1_T2_h2)

question: How do theory and research work together in nursing?

options.A: Theory replaces the need for any actual patient research
options.B: Research tests theories in practice, and practice helps shape new theories
options.C: Research only happens when there are no theories available
options.D: Theories are only used by doctors while nurses do research

explanation: Exactly! They go hand-in-hand: research tests our ideas in real life, and those findings help refine our theories. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T1#GNS217_U1_T1_h4)

question: How wide is the standard unsterile border around a sterile drape or package wrapper?

options.A: Six inches
options.B: Three inches
options.C: One inch
options.D: Twelve inches

explanation: That outer one-inch edge of any sterile wrap is considered touched and unsterile. Good rule of thumb to always remember! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T3#GNS123_U5_T3_h4)

question: Why do we have formal research guidelines like the Belmont Report in healthcare?

options.A: To help hospitals make more money
options.B: To prevent exploitation and protect human participants from harm
options.C: To guarantee positive study results
options.D: To speed up drug approvals

explanation: Exactly! Past abuses taught us that research participants need strong, guaranteed protection for their safety and rights. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T19#GNS224_U1_T19_h1)

question: Why is wearing loose cotton clothing a great tip for patients with skin issues in hot, humid weather?

options.A: It prevents topical prescription creams from rubbing off onto furniture
options.B: It minimizes trapped sweat, friction, and heat irritation on the skin
options.C: It acts as a medicated dressing that heals open wounds overnight
options.D: It completely blocks all ultraviolet radiation from reaching the epidermis

explanation: Exactly! Breathable cotton stops sweat and rubbing from building up, which keeps those pesky flare-ups at bay. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T6#GNS213_U5_T6_h7)

question: A nurse in a busy Lagos clinic wants to cut down patient waiting times without buying new computers. What is the best approach?

options.A: Complain to the patients about the lack of staff instead of changing anything
options.B: Refuse to see any patients who arrive after eight o'clock in the morning
options.C: Use a PDSA cycle to test reorganizing the patient triage and record-pulling process
options.D: Wait until the government donates brand new digital tablets to the clinic

explanation: You nailed it! Reorganizing how we do things using a quick PDSA test is a fantastic way to improve patient flow without spending money. [learn more](GST319_U3_T5#GST319_U3_T5_h7)

question: What is the main difference between cancer staging and cancer grading?

options.A: Staging measures how far the cancer has spread, while grading describes how abnormal the cells look
options.B: Staging evaluates treatment side effects, while grading measures tumor size only
options.C: Staging determines the patient's age of onset, while grading determines their genetic risk
options.D: Staging is done exclusively with blood tests, while grading requires a patient interview

explanation: Well done! Think of staging as 'where has it traveled?' and grading as 'how wild and aggressive do the cells look under a microscope?' [learn more](GNS216_U5_T33#GNS216_U5_T33_h6)

question: Research objectives need to be clear and measurable. What kind of words should they always start with?

options.A: Pronouns
options.B: Action verbs
options.C: Prepositions
options.D: Adjectives

explanation: Always kick off your objectives with active words like 'to evaluate', 'to assess', or 'to compare' so everyone knows exactly what you plan to do. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T2#GNS224_U3_T2_h4)

question: How do modern communities (like online student groups) change our view of physical borders?

options.A: Individuals can no longer feel attached to their neighborhoods
options.B: Physical maps are no longer used by any government agencies
options.C: Geographical borders completely disappear during public health emergencies
options.D: People can form connected groups based on shared interests without living near each other

explanation: Today, technology and social media let people connect and support each other across long distances, stretching beyond just physical location. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T3#GNS225_U1_T3_h2)

question: When is the best time to start a chosen birth control method after an abortion?

options.A: Only after the six-week follow-up visit
options.B: On the exact same day as the abortion procedure
options.C: After waiting for three complete menstrual cycles
options.D: When cervical mucus changes appear

explanation: Starting contraception on day one ensures the patient is protected before ovulation sneaks up on them. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T016#GNS226_U5_T016_h5)

question: Why are pencil-point spinal needles often preferred over cutting needles?

options.A: They completely eliminate the risk of infection
options.B: They are cheaper to manufacture
options.C: They inject medication twice as fast
options.D: They separate dura fibers rather than cutting them

explanation: Pencil-point needles part the dural fibers, lowering the amount of cerebrospinal fluid leakage and reducing headache risks. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T10#GNS125_U3_T10_h4)

question: Which everyday task puts women in displacement camps at high risk of physical attack?

options.A: Receiving dry food rations directly from aid workers
options.B: Attending mandatory community health education workshops
options.C: Walking long distances alone to collect firewood and water
options.D: Participating in organized camp leadership meetings during the day

explanation: Going out to fetch water or firewood means walking through lonely, unlit areas far from help. It's a huge safety hazard for women in camps. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T11#GNS312_U4_T11_h2)

question: Why is it smart for nurse managers to review staff feedback surveys about teamwork and collaboration?

options.A: To identify departmental friction points before they cause patient harm
options.B: To replace all human staff members with automated software
options.C: To decide which staff members deserve a pay cut
options.D: To eliminate the need for any future meetings

explanation: You got it! Surveys give the team a voice to point out where things are clashing, allowing managers to step in and fix things proactively. [learn more](GST321_U1_T12#GST321_U1_T12_h7)

question: What is the main job of barium sulfate during a lower GI X-ray?

options.A: Lubricate the rectal wall to ease tube insertion
options.B: Act as a contrast medium that blocks X-rays so the bowel shows up clearly
options.C: Stimulate rapid peristalsis and empty the colon
options.D: Absorb excess gas pockets inside the large bowel

explanation: Barium sulfate is a special metallic compound that X-rays cannot easily pass through. This makes the lining of the bowel stand out brightly on the image! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T9#GNS212_U1_T9_h1)

question: Which of these is a major activity of voluntary health agencies?

options.A: Passing national laws in the legislative assembly
options.B: Conducting health education and disease prevention
options.C: Arresting individuals who violate public sanitary codes
options.D: Setting official salaries for government doctors

explanation: Correct! Voluntary agencies love teaching people simple hygiene and wellness habits to stop diseases before they start. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T28#GNS225_U5_T28_h4)

question: When a patient eats a complex starch, what must happen before the body can absorb it?

options.A: It must gain extra nitrogen atoms to form a protein chain
options.B: It must be transformed into a mineral salt solution
options.C: It must be broken down into single monosaccharide rings
options.D: It must be converted directly into a complex lipid structure

explanation: Your gut can only absorb tiny, single sugar units. That is why large starches must be broken down by digestion first! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T004#GNS227_U1_T004_h2)

question: What does a low Mid-Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC) mostly point to during a community screening?

options.A: Normal muscle development
options.B: Risk of acute malnutrition
options.C: Excess visceral fat storage
options.D: Elevated serum cholesterol

explanation: Well done! MUAC is a quick, life-saving tool we use in community health to spot wasting and acute malnutrition in children and mothers. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T003#GNS227_U5_T003_h5)

question: How do you know for sure if a patient truly understood your health education instructions?

options.A: Asking the patient to explain the instructions back in their own words
options.B: Ensuring the nurse spoke clearly without using medical jargon
options.C: Writing down all the medication dosages on a whiteboard
options.D: Handing the patient a printed pamphlet before leaving the room

explanation: This is the classic 'teach-back' method! Asking them to explain it in their own words helps you catch any confusion without making them feel small. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T23#GNS225_U2_T23_h2)

question: What is a major goal of health education when a community is facing an epidemic?

options.A: Encouraging early health-seeking behavior
options.B: Discouraging people from visiting hospitals
options.C: Increasing community fear of the disease
options.D: Promoting traditional medical practices

explanation: Spot on! Good health education encourages people to report symptoms early so treatment can start before complications set in. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T89#GNS214_U1_T89_h7)

question: Why is a waste factor or buffer stock added when calculating injection commodities?

options.A: To provide extra income for the hospital pharmacy department
options.B: To ensure the facility has extra funds to pay staff salaries
options.C: To cover dropped items, training breakage, and accidental contamination
options.D: To account for patients who refuse to take their medications

explanation: A buffer percentage ensures unexpected item loss on the ward does not lead to a sudden shortage of clinical tools. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h3)

question: A community health nurse visits a home where a mother has missed two vaccine appointments. What is the best first step during the visit?

options.A: Threaten to report the family to local village authorities
options.B: Listen to the mother's reasons with empathy and offer gentle guidance
options.C: Inform the neighbors that the mother is neglecting her baby
options.D: Administer the vaccines immediately without asking any questions

explanation: A respectful, non-judgmental approach builds trust and helps uncover the real reasons behind the missed appointments. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T74#GNS214_U1_T74_h4)

question: Why is an intramuscular injection of Vitamin K given routinely to all newborns?

options.A: To prevent dangerous bleeding disorders
options.B: To boost immediate antibody production
options.C: To treat congenital eye infections
options.D: To protect against bacterial meningitis

explanation: Newborn guts are sterile and cannot make Vitamin K yet, so an injection stops life-threatening bleeding complications. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T51#GNS214_U1_T51_h7)

question: What genotype represents a person who carries the sickle cell trait without having the full disease?

options.A: SS
options.B: AA
options.C: SC
options.D: AS

explanation: Genotype AS means the individual has one normal gene and one mutated gene, making them a healthy carrier of the trait. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h2)

question: Which equipment design helps lower the chance of a spinal headache?

options.A: Atraumatic pencil-point needles
options.B: Wide-bore metal needles
options.C: Disposable plastic syringes
options.D: Flexible silicone tubing

explanation: Correct! Pencil-point needles gently push fibers aside instead of cutting them, allowing the puncture hole to seal much faster. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T9#GNS221_U2_T9_h7)

question: What is the most important infection control practice for a family caregiver managing a home gastrostomy tube?

options.A: Boiling all feeding bags in water after every single meal
options.B: Performing thorough hand hygiene before handling the tube
options.C: Cleaning the entire feeding pump machine with bleach daily
options.D: Wearing sterile surgical gloves for every single water flush

explanation: Proper handwashing is the single most effective way to prevent harmful bacteria from entering the gastrostomy site or formula bag. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h8)

question: How does smoking fish and meat help preserve the food?

options.A: It deposits natural antimicrobial smoke compounds and dries the flesh
options.B: It adds chemical nitrates that bleach the meat white
options.C: It completely seals the food inside an airtight plastic wrap
options.D: It infuses the meat with cold air to freeze internal cells

explanation: Wood smoke does double duty: the chemicals in the smoke kill off microbes, and the heat dries the meat out nicely. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T011#GNS227_U3_T011_h3)

question: A new mother on the ward is bleeding heavily two hours after delivery, and her uterus feels soft and boggy. What is the likely cause?

options.A: Eclamptic seizure
options.B: Obstructed labor
options.C: Pelvic inflammatory disease
options.D: Uterine atony

explanation: When the uterus fails to contract firmly (atony), the blood vessels stay open and bleeding happens. A firm massage and oxytocics are usually our best friends here! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T013#GNS226_U1_T013_h3)

question: What makes BMI such a popular first step in routine nursing assessments?

options.A: It provides a definitive diagnosis for metabolic syndrome
options.B: It accounts for variations in muscle mass and bone density
options.C: It is the only medically accepted way to evaluate body composition
options.D: It is quick, easy, and requires only height and weight measurements

explanation: You got this! Because you only need a patient's height and weight, BMI is super practical for busy shifts in the clinic or ward. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T10#GNS121_U1_T10_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended home care practice for managing a mild fever?

options.A: Giving prescribed doses of antipyretic medication safely
options.B: Monitoring the patient for unusual symptoms or confusion
options.C: Dressing the patient in heavy, thick blankets to trap body heat
options.D: Encouraging frequent oral intake of fluids and water

explanation: Trapping body heat with heavy blankets prevents natural cooling and can cause the temperature to rise even higher. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T3#GNS221_U3_T3_h6)

question: When we talk about 'psychosocial' care in mental health nursing, what two main things are we bringing together?

options.A: Laboratory values and physical symptoms
options.B: Emotional experiences and environmental conditions
options.C: Surgical history and genetic mutations
options.D: Medication side effects and dietary habits

explanation: Spot on! Psychosocial care looks at both sides of the coin: what is happening inside a person's mind (psychological) and what is happening in their world outside (social). [learn more](GNS314_U6_T2#GNS314_U6_T2_h1)

question: Why should a nurse check local market days and religious schedules before setting a date for a community health talk?

options.A: To comply with international trade and economic regulations
options.B: To avoid scheduling conflicts that would prevent people from attending
options.C: To make sure the weather is always cool and rainy
options.D: To ensure the nurse can buy fresh food items after the meeting

explanation: You nailed it! Checking local routines ensures you pick a time when people are actually free to show up and learn. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T1#GNS214_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why do traditional NSAIDs often give patients a grumpy stomach or ulcers after long-term use?

options.A: They block COX-1, which removes the protective lining of the stomach
options.B: They increase the production of stomach acid to dangerous levels
options.C: They directly burn the stomach wall upon contact
options.D: They stop the stomach from digesting food properly

explanation: Not all prostaglandins are bad! COX-1 makes a special lining that protects your tummy from its own acid. When NSAIDs block COX-1, that protective shield gets thin. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T4#GNS223_U5_T4_h1)

question: Which sterilization method is best suited for sharp surgical blades because it prevents them from dulling?

options.A: Boiling water for twenty minutes
options.B: Dry heat in a hot air oven
options.C: High-pressure steam autoclave
options.D: Cold soaking in mild soap water

explanation: Dry heat does not cause rust or water-related dulling, making it ideal for maintaining the sharp edges of surgical blades. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h3)

question: A new mum just had a repair for a fourth-degree tear and is terrified of her first toilet trip. What should be in her care plan?

options.A: Providing daily enemas to clear the lower bowel completely
options.B: Instructing her to restrict all oral fluid intake until she passes stool
options.C: Applying strong pressure dressings over the anus to prevent stool passage
options.D: Administering prescribed stool softeners and encouraging high-fiber foods

explanation: Soft stools mean she won't have to strain, which keeps the delicate stitches in her anal area safe and undisturbed. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h6)

question: How are purely synthetic drugs made?

options.A: Manufactured completely in laboratories using chemicals
options.B: Miners digging raw crystals out of deep caves
options.C: Extracted directly from the roots of tropical trees
options.D: Harvested from the blood serum of healthy livestock

explanation: Synthetic drugs don't come from nature at all—chemists build them from scratch inside a laboratory. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T5#GNS125_U2_T5_h5)

question: A fertility patient feels lonely and upset. What is the kindest and most professional nursing action?

options.A: Validate her feelings and offer information on support groups
options.B: Advise her to keep her struggles entirely private from family
options.C: Tell the patient to stop treatments immediately to save money
options.D: Explain that emotional stress has no impact on physical health

explanation: Listening, validating her feelings, and connecting her with others going through the same thing makes all the difference. You're learning to be a wonderful nurse! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T23#GNS312_U1_T23_h7)

question: Why is feeding through the gut (enteral nutrition) usually preferred over drips (parenteral nutrition) for surgical patients?

options.A: It preserves gut immune function and carries fewer infectious risks
options.B: It is absorbed much faster than intravenous fluids
options.C: It bypasses the digestive system entirely
options.D: It can be administered without any medical equipment

explanation: You got it! Using the natural digestive tract keeps the gut healthy and avoids the high infection risks that come with central lines. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T009#GNS227_U7_T009_h5)

question: What is an example of closed-loop communication during a resuscitation?

options.A: Calling out for extra help over the hospital public address system
options.B: Repeating an order back to the leader to confirm it was heard and understood
options.C: Nodding your head silently when the doctor walks into the room
options.D: Writing down all medications on a paper chart after the code ends

explanation: Closed-loop communication prevents dangerous mistakes by ensuring every order is clearly acknowledged and verified. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T4#GNS315_U4_T4_h8)

question: What is a major financial barrier for families of special children in Nigeria?

options.A: Mandatory free private nursing care at home
options.B: Excessive government funding for all childhood treatments
options.C: Free international travel for medical checkups
options.D: High out-of-pocket costs for therapies and medical supplies

explanation: Most families bear the financial burden of care directly because public insurance coverage for chronic disabilities is limited. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h8)

question: A community nurse wants to design a new maternal health schedule by gathering input from local mothers and clinic staff. Which leadership style is being used?

options.A: Democratic
options.B: Autocratic
options.C: Bureaucratic
options.D: Laissez-Faire

explanation: Involving stakeholders in the decision-making process is the hallmark of a democratic or participative leadership style. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T2#GNS124_U2_T2_h2)

question: A patient is given a drug that blocks acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction. What happens as a result?

options.A: Muscle relaxation and paralysis
options.B: Increased action potential speed
options.C: Rapid muscle hypertrophy
options.D: Uncontrolled muscle spasms

question: What is health economics mostly about in a healthcare system?

options.A: How to eliminate all costs for patients seeking care
options.B: How to distribute equal salaries to all healthcare workers
options.C: How limited resources are used to provide health services
options.D: How to maximize profits for private pharmaceutical companies

explanation: Think of health economics as managing limited funds and supplies so we can care for as many patients as possible. You've got this! [learn more](GST322_U3_T5#GST322_U3_T5_h1)

question: Which task is a core responsibility of a home health nurse?

options.A: Issuing legal discharge papers from the hospital
options.B: Performing major emergency surgeries in the living room
options.C: Organizing pillboxes and checking medication use
options.D: Purchasing all household groceries for the family

explanation: Medication management, such as organizing pillboxes and checking for side effects, is a daily duty for home health nurses. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T7#GNS324_U1_T7_h2)

question: What is the main job of the accessory (helper) female reproductive organs?

options.C: To filter toxins from the pelvic blood supply
options.D: To regulate the monthly menstrual bleeding cycle

question: What is the primary function of the clitoris?

options.A: Producing female hormones
options.B: Sexual arousal and pleasure
options.C: Regulating vaginal pH balance
options.D: Filtering out harmful bacteria

question: Why must local Rapid Response Centers connect with national disaster frameworks?

options.A: To eliminate the need for local emergency supplies and equipment
options.B: To ensure that hospitals never have to report patient statistics
options.C: To transfer all administrative responsibilities away from local community leaders
options.D: To ensure seamless sharing of personnel, funding, and resources across jurisdictions

explanation: When a local disaster gets too big to handle alone, connecting with national networks makes it easy to call in extra hands and supplies. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T1#GNS315_U5_T1_h6)

question: What is the primary focus of a midwife's professional practice?

options.A: Diagnosing and treating chronic non-communicable diseases
options.B: Managing complex surgical procedures in tertiary hospitals
options.C: Providing care during pregnancy, labor, and the postpartum period
options.D: Administering pediatric vaccinations exclusively

explanation: Midwives specialize in supporting women through pregnancy, childbirth, and the postnatal stage. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T15#GNS225_U3_T15_h1)

question: What is the main cause of Tumor Lysis Syndrome when cancer treatment begins?

options.A: Rapid destruction of large numbers of cancer cells releasing contents into the blood
options.B: Bacterial invasion of the bloodstream due to low white blood cell counts
options.C: Severe dehydration caused by prolonged nausea and vomiting after chemotherapy
options.D: A sudden allergic reaction to the intravenous fluids administered in the clinic

explanation: You've got this! When chemo works *too* fast, cells burst open all at once, flooding the blood with waste products that stress the kidneys. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T9#GNS321_U1_T9_h7)

question: Which of these options is a classic example of a traumatic emergency?

options.A: A bone fracture and heavy bleeding following a motor crash
options.B: A sudden stroke caused by a blocked blood vessel in the brain
options.C: A severe asthma attack triggered by dust in the ward
options.D: A sudden drop in blood sugar leading to a diabetic coma

explanation: Trauma involves physical force from the outside world, such as a vehicle crash. Great job spotting the difference! [learn more](GNS315_U2_T3#GNS315_U2_T3_h1)

question: A child raised in an environment with chronic family violence is at a higher risk for what?

options.A: Developing aggressive or defiant coping mechanisms
options.B: Developing a complete immunity to stress
options.C: Becoming overly passive and compliant
options.D: Achieving superior academic performance

explanation: Severe environmental stress teaches children unhealthy ways to handle their emotions and frustrations. Early support can help change this path! [learn more](GNS314_U2_T1#GNS314_U2_T1_h3)

question: A patient has an abnormally low BMI. What major physiological complication are they most at risk for?

options.A: Increased bone mineral density and joint stiffness
options.B: Chronic elevation of systemic blood pressure
options.C: Impaired immune function and delayed wound healing
options.D: Excessive thickening of arterial walls from plaque buildup

question: What is the main purpose of the blood-testis barrier created by Sertoli cells?

options.A: To filter out excess water from the seminal fluid
options.B: To prevent the immune system from attacking developing sperm cells
options.C: To stop bacteria from traveling upward from the urinary tract
options.D: To maintain high blood pressure inside the seminiferous tubules

question: Which of these makes a urinary tract infection automatically classified as 'complicated'?

options.B: The infection occurs in a male patient
options.C: Urinalysis shows trace amounts of blood
options.D: Symptoms started less than 24 hours ago

question: Which teaching point is vital when instructing a client on how to use male latex condoms correctly?

options.A: Advising them to put the condom on after intercourse has started
options.B: Recommending that they store the condoms in a hot car glove box
options.C: Telling them that condoms can be washed and reused three times
options.D: Instructing them to avoid using oil-based lubricants with latex

question: What term describes an increase in the total number of muscle fibers during fetal development?

question: When looking at needle sizes, what does a higher gauge number tell you?

options.C: The needle width is smaller
options.D: The barrel capacity is larger

explanation: Needle gauges can trick people, but just remember: the bigger the gauge number, the tinier and thinner the actual needle! A 27-gauge is super fine, while an 18-gauge is quite thick. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h3)

question: What does the term 'anovulation' mean in reproductive health?

options.A: Painful menstrual cramps during a normal period
options.B: The complete absence of a uterus from birth
options.C: The failure of the ovaries to release an egg
options.D: The early cessation of all menstrual bleeding

explanation: An-ovulation simply means 'without ovulation'—the cycle happens, but the ovaries don't release an egg that month. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T7#GNS121_U5_T7_h7)

question: Which special pathways let electrical signals pass straight from one heart cell to the next?

options.A: Gap junctions
options.B: T-tubules
options.C: Sarcoplasmic reticula
options.D: Desmosomes

explanation: Gap junctions act like open doors (or tunnels) that let electrical signals zoom quickly between neighbor cells, keeping your heartbeat coordinated. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T10#GNS121_U3_T10_h2)

question: What makes the measuring tape especially useful for community health nursing?

options.A: It can diagnose complex infectious diseases
options.B: It is portable, cheap, and non-invasive
options.C: It provides automated digital health records
options.D: It replaces the need for laboratory blood tests

explanation: Field tools must be easy to carry and simple to use without hurting the patient, making basic tape measures ideal for outreach work. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T9#GNS225_U2_T9_h1)

question: What do we call a cultural rule that stops people from eating certain foods in a community?

options.A: A medical prescription for a specific disease
options.B: A cultural rule that prohibits eating certain foods
options.C: A modern scientific diet plan for weight loss
options.D: A government law regulating food prices

explanation: Nutritional taboos are simply traditional or cultural rules that forbid eating certain food items based on community beliefs. You've got this! [learn more](GNS225_U6_T9#GNS225_U6_T9_h1)

question: What does the letter 'C' stand for in the popular CAGE alcohol screening tool?

options.A: Craving
options.B: Control
options.C: Chronic
options.D: Cut down

explanation: The 'C' stands for asking if the patient has ever felt they ought to Cut down on their drinking. It's a quick, friendly way to start a health chat. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T013#GNS227_U4_T013_h6)

question: What is the main goal of using an open-ended question when talking to a patient?

options.A: To let patients tell their story in their own words
options.B: To test the patient's memory on past surgeries
options.C: To get a quick yes or no answer about a symptom
options.D: To confirm the exact date a medication was started

explanation: You got it! Open-ended questions give patients the freedom to express their concerns naturally without feeling rushed or boxed in. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T1#GNS124_U6_T1_h3)

question: A patient recovering from abdominal surgery has not passed gas or had a bowel movement in three days. Which basic need is primarily affected?

options.A: Elimination
options.B: Safety and security
options.C: Love and belonging
options.D: Self-esteem

explanation: Bowel function falls under physiological elimination needs, which nurses closely monitor post-operatively. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h3)

question: You are caring for a patient with long-standing diabetes. Which assessment is key for tertiary prevention of microvascular issues?

options.A: Measuring handgrip strength using a dynamometer
options.B: Palpating superficial lymph nodes in the neck
options.C: Asking about daily recreational screen time habits
options.D: Checking urine for microalbumin and performing foot exams

explanation: Spot on! Checking urine for tiny amounts of protein (microalbumin) and inspecting the feet regularly helps catch early kidney and nerve damage. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T17#GNS222_U2_T17_h4)

question: What is a common long-term physical problem caused by having very heavy periods for a long time?

options.A: Permanent kidney failure
options.B: Iron-deficiency anemia
options.C: Broken bones
options.D: Severe adult asthma

explanation: You nailed it! Losing blood month after month empties out the body's iron reserves, leading directly to anemia. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T7#GNS311_U1_T7_h8)

question: What is the best way to handle nausea for a patient getting chemo?

options.A: Only give them if the patient asks for help
options.B: Administer them two days after treatment ends
options.C: Wait until the patient vomits twice
options.D: Give them proactively before nausea starts

explanation: Smart nursing! Preventing nausea before it starts works way better than trying to stop it after the patient is already throwing up. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T7#GNS215_U6_T7_h7)

question: What happens when Nigeria falls short of the Abuja Declaration target for health spending?

options.A: Health institutions face severe underfunding and rely on alternative funding streams
options.B: Nurses receive higher salaries from international grants
options.C: International agencies take over total control of state clinics
options.D: Private hospitals are forced to close down permanently

explanation: When public health budgets fall short, hospitals struggle with basic running costs and have to look for other ways to survive. [learn more](GST322_U3_T5#GST322_U3_T5_h2)
